I like small teams, short feedback loops and boring infrastructure that lets the product be bold. Replace this copy with your own story: where you started, what you got obsessed with, and what you want to build next.

projectsIntro.title: Selected *work*.
projectsIntro.lede: Products I have designed, built and run in production. Open any card for the full case study.

projects.title: Atlas
projects.summary: Live tracking and dispatch for 12,000 vehicles, with sub-second updates from the road to the ops dashboard.

caseStudy.heading: Problem
caseStudy.body: Dispatchers were working from a map that lagged up to 30 seconds behind reality, and the polling backend fell over at peak.

caseStudy.heading: Approach
caseStudy.body: Replaced polling with a WebSocket fan-out backed by Postgres logical replication, partitioned by region. Rebuilt the map layer to diff updates instead of re-rendering.

caseStudy.heading: Outcome
caseStudy.body: Updates land in under 400ms end-to-end. Infrastructure cost dropped 35% while handling 4× the traffic.

projects.title: Ledgerline
projects.summary: An auditable, idempotent ledger service that became the source of truth for every cent moving through the platform.

caseStudy.heading: Problem
caseStudy.body: Balances were computed from five different tables. Finance reconciled by hand every month, and every edge case was a support ticket.

caseStudy.heading: Approach
caseStudy.body: Designed an append-only double-entry model with idempotency keys and event sourcing to Kafka. Wrote property-based tests for every invariant.

caseStudy.heading: Outcome
caseStudy.body: Month-end close went from four days to an automated report. Zero balance discrepancies since launch.

projects.title: Fieldnotes
projects.summary: A local-first, multiplayer document editor that works offline and merges cleanly when you reconnect.

caseStudy.heading: Problem
caseStudy.body: Teams in the field needed to take structured notes with patchy connectivity, without overwriting each other.

caseStudy.heading: Approach
caseStudy.body: Built on Yjs CRDTs with a Redis-backed presence layer and a custom React binding that keeps renders scoped to the changed block.

caseStudy.heading: Outcome
caseStudy.body: Shipped to 3,000 field researchers; offline edits merge without conflicts.

projects.title: Pulse
projects.summary: A themeable component library and chart kit adopted by four product teams, documented down to the motion curves.

caseStudy.heading: Problem
caseStudy.body: Four teams, four button styles, and charts that broke on every new dataset.

caseStudy.heading: Approach
caseStudy.body: Token-driven theming, headless primitives with accessible defaults, and a chart grammar built on D3 scales with React rendering.

caseStudy.heading: Outcome
caseStudy.body: Teams ship UI roughly twice as fast. Accessibility audits pass by default.

projects.title: Hatch
projects.summary: A zero-config CLI that scaffolds typed full-stack apps with tests, CI and deploy targets wired up.

caseStudy.heading: Problem
caseStudy.body: Every new service started with two days of copy-pasting configs from the last one.

caseStudy.heading: Approach
caseStudy.body: Composable templates, a plugin API and snapshot-tested generators.

caseStudy.heading: Outcome
caseStudy.body: Used by teams at several companies; new services go from idea to deploy in under an hour.
